My research focuses on developing and evaluating statistical methods to address methodological challenges that arise when applying meta-analytic techniques to real-world datasets, including dependent effect sizes, selective reporting and publication bias, and design-comparable effect sizes. I am also interested in statistical methods for single-case experimental designs.

```{=html}
<div class="mb-4">
  <label for="publication-filter" class="visually-hidden">Filter publications</label>
  <input id="publication-filter" type="search" class="form-control" placeholder="Search by title, author, journal, or year" aria-controls="listing-methodological listing-applied">
  <p id="publication-filter-status" class="small text-muted mt-2" role="status"></p>
</div>
<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
  const input = document.getElementById('publication-filter');
  const status = document.getElementById('publication-filter-status');
  input.addEventListener('input', function () {
    const listings = ['listing-methodological', 'listing-applied'].map(
      id => window['quarto-listings'][id]
    );
    const query = input.value.trim();
    listings.forEach(listing => listing.search(query, [
      'listing-title', 'listing-authors', 'listing-journal', 'listing-date'
    ]));
    const count = listings.reduce((total, listing) => total + listing.matchingItems.length, 0);
    status.textContent = query ? `${count} publication${count === 1 ? '' : 's'} found across both sections.` : '';
  });
});
</script>
```
